# Figure captions (generated by make_figures.py; do not edit by hand, rerun the script)

Final file C80, public .90088 (sha 3e27d66c). One claim per figure; the number is computed by the script from repo files.
Files: figures/out/<name>.png (200 dpi), .pdf, and the CSV of the plotted numbers (<name>.csv or <name>_<part>.csv).

## F1_pipeline: The final pipeline and the data each block may read

Caption. C80 (sha 3e27d66c) is built separately for each scored month from 20 blocks. The 11 blocks that read the month's released cells all sit in the offline Tasks 1, 3 and 4; the 8 Task 2 blocks read only train months and data stamped at or before T; 7 blocks (5 state, 2 ongoing) take a March fit or a March board read of a method into April rows by a declared rule.

- Number it proves: 20 blocks: train 5, month (offline) 11, online <= T 7, March for April 7; Task 2 blocks with offline month access: 0 (asserted)
- Intervals: none (diagram)
- Data: REPORT.md section 4; docs/report/ASSEMBLY.md section 1; docs/report/FINAL_BUILD_PLAN.md section 1; docs/report/ADOPTED.md rows 1 to 35; C80 sha from artifacts/claude_ref/l_isinel/cand/c80/c_s7c_both_aprw10_c80.json.
- Notes: Access tags are a declaration drawn from those documents, checked by a rule in make_f1_f14.py (no Task 2 block has offline month access, no Task 1/3/4 block is tagged online); they are not a code audit (T5 holds the audits). Blocks are simplified: occupancy, the S lane and stage-4 details are merged into 'Late stages'.

## F2_waterfall: Where the score came from: adopted pieces C03 to C80

Caption. The public score rose +.01863 from C03 (.88225) to C80 (.90088) in 40 adopted steps; Task 1 state pieces gave +.01049, Task 2 ongoing +.00814, onset 0 on the public board (its Q0436 cells change private windows). The three largest steps: C19 ongoing ong2 (sccnn A, band) +.00451; C10 state v/q models + phys3 +.00443; C14 LSA + big stage 3 +.00130.

- Number it proves: total +.01863; state +.01049; ongoing +.00814
- Intervals: Black segment = forecast band written in the manifest before the upload (instrument CI or judgmental), dot = forecast. C77 is unread: its bar is the read of the same March rows on the sibling parent C75.
- Data: docs/report/ADOPTED.md (rows), artifacts/claude_ref/probes/manifest.csv (public reads), docs/report/board_calibration.csv (forecasts).
- Notes: Private-only steps (C74P, C80) change April rows only and are drawn as ticks.

## F3_forecast_vs_board: Offline forecasts predict the board for state pieces, not for queue pieces

Caption. Across 89 reads with a written forecast, forecast and board change agree in sign 65% of the time (Spearman 0.43). Task 1 state/physics pieces (n=32) land in their band 97% of the time with a median miss of .00004; Task 2 queue pieces (n=37) agree in sign only 38% of the time.

- Number it proves: state in band 97%, median |miss| .00004; queue sign agreement 38%
- Intervals: No intervals drawn; each point is one public read. Axes are symmetric-log (linear inside +-.0001).
- Data: docs/report/board_calibration.csv (cleaned by the rules in the Data rules section).
- Notes: 90 rows in the file; 1 row(s) without a forecast change are kept in the CSV only. Kind of change is set by explicit file-name rules (KIND_RULES in the script).

## F4_transfer_rule: Task 1 state gains learned on the target month carry at about 1x; queue forecasts do not

Caption. Task 1 state and physics pieces read at a median 1.00x their forecast (n=18). Ongoing members trained on train months read at -12.30x (n=5; two of the named member reads are negative). Ongoing adaptation looked like 1x to 4x in the 10-11 review (median 2.8x of the named reads), but the later adaptation reads have a median of -4.2x: queue forecasts are not reliable in either direction. Target-month label pieces read above their forecast (median 2.2x) because no offline test could see their full value.

- Number it proves: state 1.00x vs members -12.30x; later adaptation -4.2x
- Intervals: No intervals; each point is one board read divided by its pre-upload forecast change. Ratios outside +-30 are drawn at the edge; reads with a forecast change below .00001 are left out (listed in the CSV).
- Data: docs/report/REVIEW_2026-10-11.md section 2 table (groups and named examples); docs/report/board_calibration.csv (changes); artifacts/claude_ref/probes/manifest.csv (read dates for the later reads).
- Notes: Named state examples: C17, C20, C26, C30, C34, C38. The cold-start group is C36 plus later cold-date XSD reads. C18 (forecast 0, board -.0063) has no ratio. This record led to the 10-17 ruling to focus on state pieces (DECISIONS_DIGEST.md).

## F5_registry: Breadth and honesty of the search: every idea has a verdict class

Caption. 267 ideas were tested and classified: ADOPTED 45, REFUTED 108, UNDETECTED 80, BAD-INSTRUMENT 16, REASONING-ONLY 16, passed offline but not shipped 2. Over a third of the ideas were refuted with a stated test power; the adoption rate is about the same whether an idea learns from the target month (18%) or not (17%), because train-month ideas were screened by board reads early (F4) and stopped.

- Number it proves: adoption rate yes 18% / partly 15% / no 17%
- Intervals: Counts, no intervals.
- Data: docs/research/registry/REGISTRY.tsv (columns task, verdict_class, learns_from_target_month).
- Notes: PASS-OFFLINE (R241) and ADOPTED-candidate (R248) are shown as 'passed offline, not shipped'. learns_from_target_month variants such as 'yes (March fit)' are mapped to their first word.

## F6_spacetime: Held-out speed error on one March day is small

Caption. On D12_I405_S, 2031-03-18 (March; the day with the most released congested INEL cells, chosen by that rule), the held-out prediction at 934 INEL cells (7.4% of the grid) has speed RMSE 2.0 km/h against a released-speed SD of 18.9 km/h at the same cells; at congested INEL cells the RMSE is 1.4 km/h. Released speed values are not drawn.

- Number it proves: RMSE 2.0 km/h vs SD 18.9 km/h (INEL cells of the day)
- Intervals: No intervals; one day, one panel, all INEL cells of the day.
- Data: artifacts/cache (released cells, official view), artifacts/claude_ref/l_inelfold/isi/chain/validation/fold (INEL-FOLD chain, exp/L_inelfold/LINE.md).
- Notes: Predictions are the INEL-FOLD chain: C77-class members (FV-INEL W1.0) that took INEL labels only from the other fold, so every INEL cell shown is held out. INEL cells are released and never scored; scored target cells carry no value in the cache (asserted) and are blank. Not C80 itself (S7c is not in this chain).

## F7_fundamental_diagram: Held-out predictions are physically plausible

Caption. At 968,856 held-out INEL cells of March (10 panels), our predictions sit on the published fundamental diagram at least as closely as the released observations: FD loss (sum |q - q_FD(k)| / sum q, per lane) R1 0.010 vs 0.015, R2 0.009 vs 0.015, R3 0.009 vs 0.015 (ours vs released).

- Number it proves: R1 0.010/0.015; R2 0.009/0.015; R3 0.009/0.015
- Intervals: Hexbin counts on a log colour scale; no intervals.
- Data: artifacts/cache (released cells), artifacts/claude_ref/l_inelfold/isi/chain/validation/fold, network fd_parameters.csv through src/tfb/metric.py _parameters (the scorer replica's FD form).
- Notes: Axes are normalised per station (kc = capacity / free speed, as in the scorer), so all stations share one free-flow branch; the congested branch differs by station and the drawn one uses the median kjam/kc. Lower FD loss for ours partly reflects that predictions are smoother than observations (hypothesis).

## F8_physics_anatomy: Mass balance breaks at lone hidden cells on long links

Caption. Lone hidden cells carry 88% of the LWR conservation loss (March own view). The long-link tercile holds 70% of the physics sensitivity but only 34% of the state sensitivity; on held-out INEL cells it holds 71% of the density x length transition residual (proxy).

- Number it proves: long links: physics 70%, state 34%
- Intervals: Published point values (R5, 10% error cut per class); no intervals were computed in R5.
- Data: docs/research/ideas_R5/R5.md tables 1b and 1c (own view, C66/C69 chain); proxy bars computed here from artifacts/cache and the INEL-FOLD chain.
- Notes: The space x time map of the conservation residual named in FINAL_PLAN 4.3 needs the own-view chain grids of R5 (scratch, not in the repo); see TODO_F6_F7.md section F8. The proxy uses INEL cells, which the physics scorer does not score (they are ineligible), so it is a cross-check of the length effect only.

## F9_error_anatomy: The remaining state error lives at queue fronts on four panels

Caption. Queue-front cells are 2.2% / 2.4% of cells but hold 85% / 79% of the improvable state error (March / April); four panels hold 71% / 69% of it in 20% of cells. A tail of about 300 single-step hedges a month (speed error > 15 km/h, .031% of cells) carries 19% / 17% of the whole linear state loss.

- Number it proves: fronts 2.2% of cells, 85%/79% of improvable error
- Intervals: Published point shares; R6A reports no intervals for the slice shares.
- Data: docs/research/ideas_R6/R6A.md section 1 table (FV2 chain at INEL cells, official geometry). The scratch outputs of R6A (r6a_sum.json) are not in the repository, so the published numbers are plotted and cited.
- Notes: Improvable = error above a heteroscedastic noise floor (R6A section 0). Slices overlap.

## F10_label_dose: New label sources beat more training on the same labels

Caption. Official-view labels of the target month gave +.00041 (FV1); 6k more steps on the same labels gave +.00002 (FV2); released-but-ineligible (INEL) cells as a new label source gave +.00025, weight 1.0 +.00002, and INEL labels in a stage learner +.00007: +.00077 in total from label sources. Held out, INEL-FOLD reads the INEL class at +.00045 March and +.00018 April (board units), with 95% CIs above zero in both months.

- Number it proves: label sources +.00077 public; INEL-FOLD Apr +.00018
- Intervals: Squares and diamonds: 95% CI, joint date bootstrap (500 draws) of I-S-INEL, scaled to board units by k = 1.81. Ticks: forecast written before each upload. Panel b: mean over 30 members, no interval.
- Data: artifacts/claude_ref/probes/manifest.csv, docs/report/board_calibration.csv, artifacts/claude_ref/l_inelfold/GATE.json, exp/L_isinel/logs/s7cf_run.log (S7CF_READ), exp/L_fvinel/logs/**/FVI_INFO lines (member loss).
- Notes: Member loss at INEL cells is IN SAMPLE for the INEL-label members (they were trained on those cells); only the held-out markers in panel a are honest. Loss = .54 (dv/25)^2 + .46 (dq per lane/600)^2, the metric's per-cell form (exp/L_fvinel/fvi_step.py inel_err). The S7c step is read against the unread C77 forecast .90081.

## F11_instrument_validation: Instruments were validated before use, and their misses are reported

Caption. I-S-INEL, calibrated once on FV1 (k = 1.815), forecast the next step FV2 at +.000019 and the board read +.00002 (ratio 1.05). INEL-FOLD put the INEL class at +.00045 [+.00019, +.00070], with the board at +.00027 inside that interval. S7c read +.00007 on the board against +.00002 forecast; held out on the shipped chain it is worth +.000020 (March) / +.000016 (April), while its in-sample value +.000069 matches the board read.

- Number it proves: FV2 board/forecast 1.05; S7c held-out +.000020 vs board +.00007
- Intervals: Horizontal bars: 95% CI, joint date bootstrap (500 draws), converted to board units by k.
- Data: artifacts/claude_ref/l_isinel/GATE.json, artifacts/claude_ref/l_inelfold/GATE.json, exp/L_isinel/logs/s7cf_run.log (S7CF_READ lines), manifest and calibration for board reads.
- Notes: FV1 is the point that defines k, so it lies on y = x by construction (grey square). The S7c miss has several possible explanations (one read's variance about .00001, front-concentrated gains, stage-learner effects the instrument under-reads); none is claimed (FINAL_PLAN section 8).

## F12_seed_curve: More seeds cut variance; the gain shows up in April, not March

Caption. Going from 2 to 3 B6 seeds lowers member error at INEL cells by 2.2% (March) and 2.7% (April) on the five small panels. At the chain this is +.000093 [+.000066, +.000119] board units in April but only +.000011 [-.000016, +.000041] in March.

- Number it proves: April +.000093 vs March +.000011
- Intervals: 95% CI, joint date bootstrap (500 draws); member CIs in panel a from the same bootstrap.
- Data: artifacts/claude_ref/l_seed6/SEED6_POWER.json, member_validation.json, member_private.json; method exp/L_seed6/LINE.md (leave-one-seed-out arms, exchangeable seeds).
- Notes: 6 seeds were NOT run to the end (SEED6 step 1 paused at the end of development, 10-21); the 3 -> 6 points are the projection e(2) - e(3) = e(3) - e(6) = b/6 under exchangeable seeds, not measurements.

## F13_decode_bottleneck: Small queue gains do not show because the decode is sharp

Caption. The median official window has no cell within 0.034 (March) / 0.031 (April) of the eIoU threshold, while in-model target-month pieces move the cells near it by 0.0036 (DW-ADAPT) and 0.0013 (TODR). At the real dose DW changes 1 March / 0 April window(s); the move must be scaled x2 (March) and x5 (April) to change the 3 windows a board read needs.

- Number it proves: median distance 0.034 vs move 0.0036; windows changed at x1 = 1 (Mar)
- Intervals: Quantiles over the 40 official windows per month; no intervals.
- Data: docs/research/ideas_R4/R4.md table 1b (official windows, A3 chain + C59 Tiny decode). Counts are of changed decoded windows only; no window truth is used.
- Notes: Decode threshold = r/(1+r) with r the window's expected IoU (about .47 on official windows).

## F14_bootstrap: Date-bootstrap distributions of the last state pieces on their own instruments

Caption. On their own instruments the last state pieces are above zero at 95% in 10 of 12 piece-months; the exceptions (FV2 March, FV2 April) straddle zero (FV2 March +.000011, P>0 .68; April +.000020, P>0 .85). S7c-INEL is small but sure (+.000011 [+.000009, +.000013] March, +.000008 April), and FV-INEL W1.0 on held-out folds gives +.000249 [+.000107, +.000387] (March) and +.000099 (April).

- Number it proves: FV2 P>0 .68 / .85; S7c-INEL P>0 1.00 / 1.00; piece-months with 95% low > 0: 10 of 12
- Intervals: 95% interval = 2.5% and 97.5% quantiles of 500 joint date-bootstrap draws (seed 4701), all panels resampled together by date; one draw set per instrument and month.
- Data: draws regenerated by figures/f14_draws.py from the stored chain arms (artifacts/claude_ref/l_isinel, l_inelfold/isi, l_isinel/s7cf/isi, l_gap3 + l_gap2/g1) with the instruments' own code; point and interval equal the stored JSONs in 12 of 12 parts (F14_bootstrap_parity.csv).
- Notes: Units: I-S-INEL, INEL-FOLD and S7C-FOLD show fc = .88 (.35 dState + .45 dPhys); the gap bench shows .308 dState, its board rule. Both are S_total forecast units, not board reads (I-S-INEL board/fc k = 1.81, l_isinel/GATE.json). FV-FT on I-S-INEL is a retrospective read (the instrument came after its adoption). Missing: ADOPTED row 32 (GAP-ON-FV, board read only, no offline draws) and row 34 W1.0 alone (only inside the INEL-FOLD pair, which carries FV-INEL and W1.0 together). Pieces before row 28 are not drawn.

## Data rules

- board_calibration.csv: a row with more than 8 fields (unquoted comma in the last prose cell) gets its extra fields joined back into that cell; a numeric cell is its FIRST number; band = first two numbers; sign and in_band = first word (lower case); the remaining prose is kept as `note` in the CSVs. in_band is recomputed (band_lo <= public <= band_hi) and sign agreement is recomputed with a .00001 zero tolerance; the recomputed values are used.
- Kind of change: fixed regular expressions on the file name (KIND_RULES in make_figures.py), first match wins.
- The adopted chain (F2, T2) is the CHAIN list in make_figures.py: one entry per ADOPTED.md row in the board file, in adoption order; the level after each step is its public read, except C77 (unread; level = C76 + the read of the same rows on C75) and the private-only steps C74P and C80.
- F6, F7, F8 proxy: released cells only; predictions = INEL-FOLD chain at held-out INEL cells; the script asserts that the cache holds no value at scored target cells.
